scope: Operator-only trusted control update, recovery and rollback

checks.note: Affected install/CLI regression selected earlier during implementation; concurrent dependency/first-install work is recorded separately.

fixture: Windows temporary filesystem, substituted systemd/process/secure snapshot operations; real generated-bootstrap subprocess verifies pending transaction rejection before legacy imports.
coverage: Independent original active and enabled service sets; gateway-only does not start the previously stopped worker
Initialized instance with no current application release stays stopped
Durable shell launch blockers installed before any control directory rename
Known management/build transients included; exact instance matching excludes longer instance names
Uncertain cgroup stop and escaped account process retain code, transaction and barriers
Startup, health, reload and integrity failures; interrupted phase and rename recovery
Legacy root-owned bytecode cache writes resealed after stop; fixed rollback bootstrap disables future cache writes
Verified edge executable tree and metadata bindings retained, including later edge installation during Python rollback
Collision preflight leaves no pending transaction or unavailable helper
Operator CLI source-argument rejection and fixed bootstraps; root ownership and RPC allowlist boundaries inspected in code

findingsFixed: Legacy bytecode cache could prevent failed rollback recovery
Previously queued management transient required a durable launcher barrier
Drop-in collision could create pending transaction and block otherwise healthy RPC
Nested old-tree files and directories required fsync before sealing and rename

notExercised: Real Linux systemd conditions, transient scheduling and complete /proc visibility
Actual host reboot or physical power-loss durability
Real active-instance control upgrade/rollback or external login/provider/MCP calls
